Bad Conditional Reasoning

Bad Conditional Reasoning occurs when the author reads the conditionals supplied in the premises incorrectly.

The Play-By-Play

1. There are conditional premises

2. Crazy person concludes something by reading the conditional premises backwards without negating.

OR

1. There are conditional premises

2. Crazy person concludes something by negating the conditional premises and reading it forwards.

Bad Causal Reasoning

The vast majority of causal conclusions on the LSAT are bad. Looking for Bad Causal Reasoning is really just looking for causal reasoning — as soon as you see it, the Omitted Options should start popping into your head.

The Play-By-Play

1. Crazy person sees that two things are correlated.

2. Crazy person concludes that one of those things is causing the other.
